The OOS split harness partitions historical picks into in-sample and out-of-sample cohorts using an immutable timestamp boundary. In-sample data is used for model calibration while out-of-sample data evaluates predictive performance. The core operator 'window_calibration' computes Brier scores for each cohort, which measure forecast accuracy. A derived metric 'brierDelta' compares these scores to detect overfitting. If the out-of-sample Brier exceeds in-sample by more than 3%, the model is flagged as unhealthy. This mechanism ensures that only models demonstrating consistent performance across unseen data are promoted. The system enforces invariance through immutability of cohort boundaries and purity of metrics. Failure modes include insufficient sample sizes leading to invalidity, or excessive Brier deterioration indicating overfitting. These checks form a dual logic: one for model integrity and another for operational robustness.
